name: timetracker-desktop
description: Desktop screenshot tracker for the Timetracker web app
_comment_version: 0.4.10 — CRITICAL installer fix: the NSIS customCheckAppRunning macro ran `taskkill /F /IM "SA Track.exe" /T`. During an auto-update the installer is SPAWNED BY SA Track.exe, so /T (kill the whole child tree of matched processes) could kill THE INSTALLER ITSELF between its uninstall and install phases. On the 0.4.7->0.4.9 hop (2026-07-31) this UNINSTALLED THE APP ACROSS THE ENTIRE FLEET and never reinstalled it: install dir emptied, registry entry gone, staged update orphaned - trackers silent for 9 days while staff clocked via the website. Standalone (double-click) installs always worked, which is why it looked fine in testing. Fix: drop /T; /IM alone matches every Electron helper (same exe name) but can never match the differently-named installer. Recovery from the wipe is MANUAL - a machine with no app cannot auto-update; each PC reinstalls once from timetracker.sparkingasia.com/download. Previous: 0.4.9 — FRESHNESS: an extension installed at 09:05 used to stay invisible on the compliance dashboard until ~10:05, because the only routine trigger was an HOURLY timer. Now the agent polls each Chrome/Edge/Brave profile's `Secure Preferences` + `Extensions` mtime every 60s and uploads as soon as anything changes (install, remove, enable, disable), the floor interval is 15 min instead of 60, and a call swallowed by the 90s upload debounce RE-ARMS instead of vanishing (otherwise a change landing just after a routine run waited for the next tick — exactly the latency this removes). Deliberately mtime polling, NOT a recursive fs.watch on `User Data`: that tree also carries caches/history/cookies which churn constantly, so a watch fires thousands of times a minute on a 27-profile machine for changes nobody cares about, and its handle dies when the browser self-updates. Measured cost of the poll on a real 27-profile machine: 21.7ms per minute. Previous: 0.4.8 — Chrome PROFILE ATTRIBUTION + a silent-data-loss fix. People here run 20-30 Chrome profiles on one PC (often one per Upwork account), so 'a scraper on PC-VA-7' was not actionable — you could not tell which profile, therefore which Upwork account, was at ban risk. Extensions now carry `browser_profile`, the switcher label from Chromium's Local State info_cache ('Upwork Misbah'), falling back to the directory name. ALSO FIXES a real defect: dedup keyed on browser+id alone, which collapsed every copy of an extension to whichever profile enumerated FIRST — and 'Default' always sorts first — so an extension present in both Default and 'Upwork Faryal' was reported as living only in Default. That is a false all-clear on the exact profile at risk; verified on a 27-profile machine where 4 real Instant Data Scraper installs were being reported as 1. Key is `browser_profile`, never `profile`: the host WAF has an HTTP-Parameter-Pollution rule on the exact name `profile` (probed unauthenticated against prod, where the WAF answers before Laravel: `profile` x40 => plain-text 403, `browser_profile` x500 with real labels => 401, i.e. passes). Labels are employee-typed free text, so `<>` is stripped (a separate XSS rule 403s the whole upload on angle brackets); non-ASCII is kept, Urdu/Arabic names verified fine. Only info_cache `name` is read — `gaia_name`/`user_name` can hold the account EMAIL and are never collected. Previous: 0.4.7 — CRITICAL upload fix: the agent sent the Chrome PROFILE DIRECTORY NAME with every extension, and Hostinger firewall blocks any request body carrying a repeated `profile` field (standard ModSecurity rule). Any machine with ~20+ extensions had its ENTIRE inventory upload rejected with a plain-text 403 — extensions, programs, processes and network all lost together — which is why over half the fleet showed no compliance data at all. The field was never used by the server (matching is by name, dedup by browser+id), so it is simply no longer sent. Previous: 0.4.6 — CRITICAL extension-inventory fix: 0.4.5 filtered extensions on `state === 1`, a field current Chrome/Edge no longer set (always undefined), so it silently dropped 100% of browser extensions — scrapers and refresh tools were invisible. Enabled-detection now reads Chromium's `disable_reasons` (array/bitmask) with `state` as a legacy fallback and DEFAULTS TO ENABLED on an unknown shape, so it can never silently drop everything again; telemetry reports kept/raw (ext=12/58). Also: 'Restart now' no longer hangs (before-quit waited on tracker.stop() with no timeout, so the app never exited and the update never applied), differential download disabled, and updater errors report to diagnostics. Previous: 0.4.5 — Machine Compliance quality pass: inventory only ENABLED, on-disk extensions (drops disabled + account-synced ghosts); run a collection right after sign-in and clock-in (not just the launch timer) so a manned PC reliably reports; report every run outcome (sent/skip/empty/failed) to diagnostics so a silent machine is diagnosable. Server side: name-only blocklist matching (no more permission-driven false VPN flags), only auto-refresh/scraper/jiggler tools alert, VPNs/automation are recorded-not-alerted, and a durable machine_flags ledger alerts once per install with Acknowledge/Ignore.

extendInfo.NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: Timetracker reads the active application name to record work activity.
